title: BSI C5:2026 to Grundschutz++
description: The 168 criteria of the Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5:2026 (machine-readable release 1.0.1, BSI), one source per criterion (basic and additional criteria together). The six general conditions (GC) for the report are not requirements on the service and are left out. C5:2026 carries no references to ISO/IEC 27001, so each criterion names the Annex A controls it corresponds to; the Grundschutz++ targets of those controls come from the BSI's own mapping. Direct targets cover what Annex A lacks, notably ISMS clauses 4 to 10. The step from each criterion to ISO and the direct targets are a draft written with AI assistance and not yet reviewed by a person. C5 is published under CC BY-ND 4.0: only criterion IDs are reused here, every remark is our own wording.

source.title: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5:2026, machine-readable release 1.0.1 (CC BY-ND 4.0)

maps.remarks: Documented framework for identifying, owning and tracking assets; inventory-related Annex A control plus GS++ asset procedure.
Maintained, logged inventory of hardware and software assets with risk data and per-resource user access lists.
Hardware inventory entries with identification, lifecycle and ownership details.
Software inventory incl. used components and supplier security-update horizon; SBOM-type requirements in GS++.
Rules for acceptable, secure use of assets across acquisition, operation, maintenance and disposal.
Risk-based approval of new production hardware after checking secure configuration.
Decommissioning procedure ensuring data deletion or media destruction before disposal or reuse.
Personnel commitment to proper handling of assets, provable return at exit, revocation if not returned.
Classification and labelling by protection needs, annual review; device identification for authentication.
Secure storage and protection of production hardware temporarily not in use.
Authorised, documented and secure transfer of production hardware to other locations.
Controls on endpoint devices and removable media (restriction, encryption, firewall, DLP).
Business continuity management system per ISO 22301/BSI 200-4 with top-management ownership; GS++ BCMS requirements fit directly.
Business impact analysis for the cloud service, reviewed annually or after significant changes.
BIA-based business continuity plans, reviewed annually; GS++ covers recovery, continuation plans and crisis organisation.
Annual testing and exercising of continuity plans involving customers and third parties, feeding results back.
Identifying and documenting legal, regulatory, contractual and self-imposed security requirements and compliance procedures.
Multi-year risk-based audit programme and audit planning avoiding operational impact; Annex A lacks programme detail, GS++ PERF.3 covers it.
Annual independent internal ISMS audits with risk treatment of findings.
Reporting security performance to top management and management review; a clause 9.3 topic absent from Annex A, matched by GS++ PERF.4.
Layered network attack detection and prevention feeding a SIEM, blocking unknown devices.
Defined security requirements for internal network connections and zone separation.
Security zones for trusted/untrusted networks, connection monitoring, annual configuration review and port/protocol justification.
Security gateways at every network perimeter, optionally redundant, with assessed cross-network access.
Separate, MFA-protected administration and orchestration networks isolated from tenant networks.
Network-level separation of tenant traffic in shared environments, physically or via encryption.
Current network topology documentation, data storage locations and annual review.
Policy and safeguards protecting data in transit against interception or manipulation, regularly reviewed.
Crypto policy: state-of-the-art algorithms, key handling rules, crypto agility, PQC strategy; Annex A crypto use plus Grundschutz++ established-algorithm requirements.
Impact evaluation, traceable documentation and staff briefing for changes to cryptographic systems; change management applied to crypto.
Periodic and incident-driven audit of encryption, authentication and key management against state of the art.
Encryption and authentication of data in transit over public networks and for remote admin access; Grundschutz++ transport encryption requirements add detail.
Encrypting customer data at rest with customer-controlled keys, agreed key procedures, and crypto protection on media reuse.
Secure key generation using sound random bit generators; Grundschutz++ key generation requirements cover algorithms, length, systems and randomness.
Risk-based schedule for rotating keys aligned with the crypto policy; Grundschutz++ covers expiry checks and no use after expiry.
Secure issuance and obtaining of public-key certificates incl. identity checks; maps to Grundschutz++ key certification requirements.
Authorised, verified provisioning and activation of keys with time-limited validity periods.
Protected key storage separated from application layers, controlled access, optional HSM based on risk.
Secure archiving of keys with restricted access; only the generic Annex A key management control applies.
Controlled, reviewed and approved key state transitions such as suspension and reinstatement.
Restricting compromised keys to decryption/verification and promptly notifying affected customers.
Deactivating expired keys so they are no longer used for encryption or signing; Grundschutz++ covers expiry and decommissioning.
Dedicated safeguards for using and distributing pre-shared keys and wildcard certificates.
Continuity of key management: HSM key backup versus redundancy assessment and recovery of lost keys.
Monitoring and recording the full key lifecycle and status changes; Grundschutz++ key directory with certification and revocation status.
Secure integration of external key management systems: certification, access control, rotation, logging, vulnerability handling.
Bring-your-own-key handling: secure import, logging and access control for customer-managed keys.
Secure development policy over the lifecycle, architecture limiting provider access to customer data, preference for certified products.
Contractual security requirements, risk assessment and supervision for outsourced development.
Documented change management policy covering risk categorisation, testing, approval and rollback of changes.
Role-based training on secure development, delivery tooling and pipeline risks.
Security feature design documentation based on security analysis, including specified inputs, outputs and errors.
Risk assessment and prioritisation of changes, mitigation for high-risk changes, customer information before release.
Risk-based, documented testing of changes and security features, anonymised test data, pre-launch penetration tests.
Access-controlled change tooling with traceable logging of all production changes to individuals.
Version control protecting source code integrity, attributing changes and enabling rollback of components.
Criteria-based approval of changes before production release, with customer involvement as agreed.
Risk-based protection of development and test environments including backup coverage.
Separation of production from non-production environments and no reuse of production secrets elsewhere.
Maintaining software component lists (SBOM) for developed and integrated software; Annex A lacks SBOM, Grundschutz++ has it.
Policy for third-party and open-source software, dependency lists, trusted sources and authenticity checks.
Handling exceptions and emergency changes within change management; Grundschutz++ has explicit emergency change rules.
Background screening before hiring and role changes, risk-classified sensitive positions; GS++ adds trustworthiness tests and periodic re-checks for critical roles.
Employment terms covering legal requirements, policy compliance, confidentiality, and documented acknowledgement of policies before data access.
Role-based, regularly updated security awareness and training with measured learning outcomes; GS++ adds effectiveness measurement and role-specific training.
Documented disciplinary process for policy or legal violations, communicated to staff and recorded when applied.
Informing staff which security duties persist after termination or change of employment.
Confidentiality agreements for staff and service organisations, based on protection needs and reviewed annually.
Documented policy for protecting information during remote work.
Technical and organisational measures enabling compliant remote working, including endpoint protection.
Role-based authorisation framework and identity/access policy; monthly access log review as add-on.
Procedures for granting and changing identities and rights, incl. break-glass accounts.
Risk-based locking for inactivity or brute force and monitoring of compromised credentials.
Timely adjustment or revocation of access rights on role change, with fixed deadlines.
Periodic review of identities and rights, deviation handling and orphan resource prevention.
Personalised, time-limited privileged access, logging and monitoring, MFA, PAM with just-in-time elevation.
Partitioning of customer data and notification or consent for provider personnel access; cloud-specific transparency.
Authentication of provider personnel and components with mandatory MFA and lockout after failed attempts.
Secure allocation, protection and reset of authentication information and password rules.
ISMS conforming to ISO/IEC 27001 with scope and documentation; lies in main clauses, so GS++ ISMS requirements.
Top-management information security policy, communicated internally and to customers.
Shared security responsibility model defining provider/customer interfaces, reviewed and communicated.
Risk-based segregation of conflicting duties with compensating controls and inventory of conflicts.
Collection and analysis of threat information feeding into risk management.
Contacts with authorities and interest groups, specifically BSI situation centre for public sector customers.
Documented risk management policy and methodology; ISO 27001 main clause topic, mapped to GS++ risk method.
Annual risk assessment, result sharing and owner review; main-clause topic covered by GS++ risk requirements.
Prioritised risk treatment plan, residual risk acceptance by owners, shared risks to customer controls.
Security risks assessed and treated in projects. The BSI targets of ISO 5.8 are no longer in the catalog; the security bodies take part instead.
Capacity and resource planning with demand forecasting so agreed service levels hold under constraints.
Monitoring of capacity, provisioning and SLA adherence; customer reporting of capacity breaches.
Customer-side control of allocated resources and notification of significant security changes.
Documented anti-malware policy for provider-managed system components.
Deployment, daily signature updates, reporting and configuration monitoring of malware protection.
Backup and restore policy by data sensitivity; Annex A backup control fits directly.
Monitoring of backup execution and timely handling of backup failures; Grundschutz++ backup success checks.
Annual restore tests against RTO/RPO, documented, in protected environments; restore-test requirements match.
Backups held at a remote site with equal protection and encrypted transfer; separate/geo-redundant storage requirements.
Policy governing event logging and monitoring for provider-managed components.
Purpose-bound handling of derived and account data, incl. stripping personal data from logs.
Technical enforcement of restricted access, retention and deletion of log and derived data.
SIEM integration with automated correlation, anomaly detection and alerting into incident handling.
Central tamper-proof log retention, deletion after purpose, authenticated encrypted log transport.
Tenant-level traceability, timestamps and forensic capability with evidence chain; forensics requirements added.
Logging infrastructure access limited to authorised admins with multi-factor authentication and controlled changes.
Availability monitoring and resilience of logging/monitoring components with automatic failure alerts.
Vulnerability handling policy with severity-based response times and risk-accepted exceptions.
Policy for detecting and managing incidents and service crashes.
Recording, classifying, prioritising and resolving incidents per the defined procedure.
Detection, recording and handling of crashes of components or the whole service.
Risk-based annual penetration testing with CVSS rating, root-cause and prior-exploitation analysis.
Periodic measurement and quarterly review of vulnerability and incident handling effectiveness.
Keeping affected cloud customers informed and involved during and after incident resolution.
Monthly or daily vulnerability scanning, severity rating, timed remediation and SIEM rule updates.
Documented hardening baselines, image checks and monitoring of hardening compliance.
Patch management policy aligned with change management, incl. post-patch scanning.
Implementing technical and organisational measures for patch deployment.
Tracking updates and vulnerabilities of third-party and open-source libraries; SBOM requirements fit.
Risk-based policy for separating data between tenants and from the provider.
Implementing, monitoring and reviewing tenant separation on shared resources, partly via cryptography.
Confidential computing (data-in-use protection) policy; Annex A covers only the cryptographic aspect.
Cryptographically rooted remote attestation for confidential computing; only loosely covered by cryptography control.
Container lifecycle policy: inventory, malware checks, hardening, signing and monitoring.
Implementing container lifecycle management measures per the policy.
Secure, standardised service interfaces, customer data export, application firewall and identity provider federation; portability lacks Annex A coverage.
Contract terms for returning customer data at termination: scope, format, timing; Grundschutz++ portability and exit requirements.
Forensically secure deletion of customer data at contract end with proof of deletion.
Security zones and risk-based physical/environmental requirements for premises and data centres, incl. autonomy times and controls at hosting providers.
Service delivery from at least two separated sites with tested redundancy meeting SLA availability.
Solid building shell, break-in resistance, intrusion detection and trained response; GS++ details perimeter, burglary resistance and alarm systems.
Preventive and detective physical entry controls with electronic, logged access control system.
Structural, technical and organisational protection against fire, smoke, lightning and water; GS++ fire and water protection requirements match closely.
Protecting power, cooling and telecom supply: UPS/generators, line inspections, redundancy, maintenance agreements.
Monitoring utility and environmental parameters with automatic alerting when thresholds are exceeded.
Risk-based documented security requirements for office workplaces.
Provider publishes secure-use guidance and complementary customer controls; Annex A only covers cloud use from customer side.
Vulnerability identification in development (SAST, DAST, code review, pentests) and remediation.
Informing customers about known vulnerabilities with CVE/CVSS, SBOM-based, CSAF disclosure.
Customer-facing logging and error handling of security-relevant events, protected and exportable.
Service offers enforceable multi-factor authentication for customer users and components.
Secure session management with invalidation of inactive sessions.
Password confidentiality procedures and tools offered to customers; verified credential distribution.
Role and rights framework for customer users supporting least privilege and access reviews.
Authorisation checks on service functions, validated before release; attribute-based option.
Software-defined networking functions protect customer data confidentiality and are validated.
Customer control over VM/container images and integrity checks at startup and runtime.
Processing and storage only in contractually agreed regions; notification of region changes.
Incident management policy, CSIRT, customer notification channels and forensic data collection procedures.
Approved incident response plans covering all phases, reviewed at least annually.
Classification, prioritisation and root-cause analysis of events, external responders, secure evidence archiving; GS++ adds forensics provider and exercises.
Documenting incident resolution and providing incident information to affected customers.
Obligation of staff and partners to report security events, without penalty for false alarms, and communicated reporting channels.
Measuring incidents, knowledge base of incidents and fixes, and learning to prevent recurrence.
Uniformly structured, version-controlled, approved and communicated policies and procedures.
Annual and event-driven review and management approval of security policies.
Register of policy exceptions with risk-based approval, validity limits and review.
Policies for controlling and monitoring service organisations, incl. independent assurance reports or audit rights for subservice organisations.
Risk assessment of service organisations before engagement, reviewed annually; GS++ adds supplier relationship classification.
Restricting supplier and subservice access to customer data and obtaining customer authorisation before engaging processors.
Maintained, annually reviewed register of service organisations contributing to the cloud service.
Risk-based monitoring of service organisations' compliance via reports and certificates, handling deviations and informing customers of adverse changes.
Exit strategies for critical purchased services aligned with continuity plans; Annex A weak, GS++ covers orderly termination, alternatives and transition.
Transparency on data flows, interfaces and responsibilities with service organisations, documented and reviewed annually.
Preventing direct exchange between suppliers and their functional components; CSP authorises and traces content transferred either way.

unmapped.reason: Legal vetting of government data access requests before disclosure has no counterpart in Annex A or Grundschutz++.
Notifying customers about government investigation requests is not addressed in Annex A or Grundschutz++.
Limiting or pseudonymising data disclosed to authorities in investigations is not addressed by Annex A or Grundschutz++.
Publishing technical procedures for disclosure to authorities to customers has no Annex A or Grundschutz++ counterpart.
